newsitem.title: USA: Sinatra improving after bout with pneumonia - report.
newsitem.headline: Sinatra improving after bout with pneumonia - report.

text.p: Legendary entertainer Frank Sinatra has been battling a slight case of pneumonia but is now feeling better, a leading Hollywood columnist reported on Tuesday.

Daily Variety's Army Archerd wrote in his column that he spoke to Sinatra's daughter, Nancy Sinatra, after she had visited her father in the hospital and she said he had a minor bout of pneumonia but that his condition had improved.
Sinatra's publicist and a hospital spokesman had earlier denied that the 80-year-old singer had anything more than a "pinched nerve" when he was admitted to Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre on Friday.

Various news reports said Sinatra was suffering from afflictions ranging from heart trouble to pneumonia. He was originally expected to return home sometime last weekend, but doctors then extended his hospital stay without explanation.
Sinatra's daughter, Tina, told Archerd the singer had been suffering from the pinched nerve "for several weeks" before being admitted. She said "he's cranky and wants to go home."
Sinatra's spokeswoman said on Tuesday that he had "personally requested there be no comment on his condition until he is released." She declined to say when he was expected to leave the hospital.
